about.title: How our ministry started
about.descr: Beeza is a humble children's center located in Tsemay. The center started on September 28, 2022 in Tsemay (Luqa) by bringing sixteen children from scattered pastoralist settlements of different backgrounds into the center, with the help of missionaries.
list: Began with sixteen children from scattered pastoralist communities.
Rooted in the Gospel — discipling children within their own context.

need.title: Every child is a gift — none is a curse
need.lead: South Omo is a region of rich cultural diversity and natural resources, yet it faces significant socio-economic challenges. In parts of the region, the traditional belief known as Mingi has labelled some children as cursed, leaving them abandoned or at risk.
need.response: We respond with the love of Christ: a safe home, daily care, education, and a family where every child is known by name.

story.title: Light for those living in darkness
story.descr: Omo Beeza Ministry is a Christ-centered initiative based in the South Omo region of Southern Ethiopia. We raise generations in a safe and loving environment where they can grow physically, emotionally, and spiritually.
story.name: “Omo” refers to the local people, while “Beza” means “light” in the Tsemay language — our prayer that the gospel will bring light to those living in darkness.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.descr: Equip the youth of South Omo through holistic education and spiritual discipleship by:
list: Equip: Educating South Omo’s youth through scriptural foundations, academic excellence, and vocational skills.

Train: Developing the next generation of leaders to serve both the Church and the wider community.

history.title: A journey of faithfulness
history.lead: From sixteen children and a step of faith, to a growing family across Luka and Bodi.

items.title: The beginning
items.descr: The Beeza Children's Center was established in the Tsemay area. Our first step was welcoming sixteen children from various pastoralist communities, in collaboration with missionary organizations.

items.title: Luqa — a strategic location
items.descr: Luqa, 63 kilometers from Jinka, is home to a significant concentration of Tsemay natives alongside a diverse population including the Banna people.

items.title: Kindergarten & farm
items.descr: Beeza Kindergarten opened its doors to young learners, and community believers helped plough and sow our 0.7-hectare farm with corn.

items.title: A growing family
items.descr: We now shelter 33 children in Luka and Bodi, with 22 children learning at Beeza Kindergarten — and we are praying toward a permanent Home Center.

region.title: Rich in heritage, hungry for hope
paragraphs: The South Omo region, while rich in cultural heritage and natural resources, faces significant socio-economic challenges.

Despite missionary engagement spanning over six decades, the region still experiences limitations in community leadership and spiritual maturity — alongside cultural challenges, educational deficiencies, and poverty.

hero.title: Frequently Asked Questions
hero.lead: Answers to common questions about our ministry, giving, and getting involved.

items.a: Omo Beeza Ministry is a locally established, Christ-centered ministry dedicated to the holistic development of vulnerable children and youth in South Omo, Ethiopia. The ministry began on September 28, 2022, in Tsemay (Luqa) with sixteen children from scattered pastoralist settlements.
“Omo” refers to the local people, while “Beza” means “light” in the Tsemay language — our prayer that the gospel will bring light to those living in darkness.
Our work is centered in Luqa, about 63 kilometers from Jinka in the Tsemay area of South Omo. Our children are sheltered in Luka and Bodi, and our office is in Jinka.

Mingi is a traditional belief in parts of South Omo under which certain children are considered cursed. Such children have historically been abandoned or put at risk. We believe every child is a gift from God, and we provide a safe, loving home for children in need.

items.q: What do you provide for the children?
items.a: We care for the whole child: shelter, nutritious meals, healthcare and emotional support, schooling and vocational skills, and Christian discipleship within a loving family.

Donors in Ethiopia can give directly by bank transfer to our Berhan Bank account (Omo Beeza Ministry, 1601160116595). You can also use the donation form on our Donate page — your email app opens with your pledge and our team follows up with the best way to complete your gift.

items.q: Can I give from outside Ethiopia?
items.a: Yes. Online card payment is coming soon. In the meantime, please submit the donation form or email us at info@omobeezaministry.com and we will help you find the best way to give.
Yes — choose “Monthly” on the donation form. Regular gifts help us plan ahead and provide consistent care for the children.

items.q: How will my gift be used?
items.a: Gifts provide food, shelter, education, and medical care for the children, and help build our Home Center and equip Beeza Kindergarten. We are committed to transparent, accountable stewardship of every gift.

items.q: How can I pray for the ministry?
items.a: Our current prayer requests are listed on the Get Involved page. You can also subscribe to updates at the bottom of any page to receive news and prayer requests.

items.q: Can I volunteer or work with you?
items.a: We welcome people with a heart for children in teaching, healthcare, administration, and outreach. Visit our Careers page to see openings or submit a general-interest application.

items.q: Can my church or organization partner with you?
items.a: Yes! We collaborate with churches, ministries, and organizations that share our vision. Please contact us to start a conversation.
Visits are arranged in advance with our team so that the children's routines and wellbeing are protected. Please contact us before planning a trip.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Omo Beeza Ministry respects your privacy. This policy explains what information we receive through this website and how we use it.

sections.title: Information you share with us
body: Our contact, prayer, application, newsletter, and donation forms do not store your information on this website. When you submit a form, your own email app opens with a pre-filled message, and the information reaches us only if you choose to send that email.
When you email or call us, we receive the details you choose to share, such as your name, email address, phone number, and message.

sections.title: How we use your information
body: We use your information only to respond to you, to process and acknowledge gifts, to send updates you have asked for, and to consider applications to serve with us. We do not sell or rent your personal information.

sections.title: Cookies and third-party services
body: This website does not use advertising or analytics cookies. The map on our Contact page is provided by Google Maps, and links to social networks lead to services with their own privacy policies.

sections.title: Children's privacy
body: Protecting the children in our care is a priority. We share images and stories thoughtfully and avoid publishing details that could identify a child's location or put them at risk.

sections.title: Your choices
body: You may ask us at any time to update or delete the information you have shared with us, or to stop sending you updates, by emailing info@omobeezaministry.com.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: By using the Omo Beeza Ministry website, you agree to these terms.

sections.title: Use of this website
body: This website shares information about our ministry and ways to support it. Please use it lawfully and respectfully.

sections.title: Content and images
body: Text, photographs, and logos on this website belong to Omo Beeza Ministry unless stated otherwise. Out of care for the children we serve, please do not copy or republish photographs without our written permission.

sections.title: Donations
body: Gifts are voluntary and support the ministry's work with children in South Omo. Our team will confirm the details of your gift with you directly. If you have any question about a gift, please contact us.

sections.title: External links
body: Links to other websites are provided for convenience. We are not responsible for the content or practices of those websites.

sections.title: Changes and contact
body: We may update these terms from time to time. Questions can be sent to info@omobeezaministry.com.
